definition: The standard score-free method for merging ranked lists from multiple retrievers: sum 1/(k + rank) across lists.
details: The standard score-free method for merging ranked lists from multiple retrievers: sum 1/(k + rank) across lists. Robust because it ignores incomparable raw scores.

explainer.lead: Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges ranked lists from several retrievers by summing 1/(k + rank) across lists. It matters because it needs no scores, only ranks, so incomparable retrievers can be combined robustly.

tiers.eli5: Like averaging contestants' finishing positions across several races instead of comparing their raw times.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers fuse results from multiple rankers by adding reciprocal ranks and re-sorting the pool. A pitfall is treating the fused score as calibrated relevance, when it is only a ranking device.
tiers.paperLevel: Score-free fusion: for each item, sum 1/(k + rank) across the lists containing it. Robust because raw scores from different retrievers are ignored as incomparable.

explainer.example: A document ranked 2nd by one retriever and 5th by another gets 1/(k+2) + 1/(k+5), which is compared against the sums for all other documents.
